data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The distinction between independent and uncorrelated failures is epistemological, not ontological: we can only observe a failure as 'independent' until a shared cause is discovered, meaning the resilience of decentralization is always a temporary, revisable hypothesis.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If a complete physical model of all interactions is available, independence can be established definitively, making the distinction ontological.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If one adopts a strictly instrumentalist view, the distinction is meaningless and only the observed correlation matters.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"There is no finite set of observations that can prove true independence, as there could always be an unobserved shared cause (e.g., a shared cosmic ray source, a shared supply chain vulnerability). Therefore, the claim of independence is a theoretical commitment, not an empirical fact. Evidence distinguishes 'uncorrelated' from 'independent' only by shifting the burden of proof: we treat failures as independent until a shared cause is found, at which point we revise our model. Resilience is thus a function of our ignorance, not just the system's structure.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
